name: Seed backlog ingestion endpoint
description: Build POST /api/admin/self-generation/seed-backlog, a small cron-secret-gated Flask route in dmai_core_complete.py that reads a JSONL file (default data/self_gen_backlog.jsonl), and for each row inserts (or upserts, keyed on capability id) a row into the capabilities table using the post-PR-HH schema: provenance='gap_driven', runtime_mode='stub', judge_confidence from the row, capability_type, name, description, and source metadata preserved in a notes/description field. This is the one manually-implemented bootstrap step that lets the rest of the backlog be picked up and materialised autonomously by the existing fresh-blood -> self-judge -> promoter -> materialiser chain. Chicken-and-egg: self-gen cannot ingest its own backlog until this endpoint exists, so this item must be built by a human PR, not by self-gen itself.
target_kpi: Endpoint returns 200 and inserts N rows matching N lines in self_gen_backlog.jsonl, verified by SELECT COUNT(*) FROM capabilities WHERE provenance='gap_driven' after a single POST call
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/admin/self-generation/seed-backlog accepts an optional ?path= query param, defaults to data/self_gen_backlog.jsonl
Endpoint is gated by _require_cron_auth() consistent with other admin endpoints (PR M pattern)
Each row is inserted idempotently (re-running the endpoint does not duplicate rows already present with the same gap id)
Endpoint returns a JSON summary: {inserted: N, skipped_existing: M, errors: [...]}
blocker: None — ready to build now; nothing else in the backlog can be auto-ingested until this lands
notes: ~50 LOC per the task brief's own estimate. Must touch dmai_core_complete.py to register the route, so it cannot be self-gen'd; this is the deliberate one human PR that unblocks everything else.

This is the exact scale-mismatch class of bug that issue #219 is meant to solve generally, but a standalone hotfix to the specific rendering path is lower-risk and faster than waiting for the full metric-contract-audit framework to land.
target_kpi: Dashboard header SI percentage is within 2 percentage points of si_overall_score * 100 on every page load, verified by an automated check
acceptance_criteria: Identify the exact render/formatter call path for the SI headline percentage

Add a regression test asserting the invariant abs(displayed_pct - si_overall_score*100) < 2.0
blocker: None — standalone hotfix, does not need to wait for #219's full framework
notes: This is a semantics fix to existing rendering code, not a net-new module, so it falls outside self-gen's net-new-only scope per #218.

name: Capability value gate (evaluation / gap-analysis system)
description: With 20,694+ capability rows and heavy likely duplication (one category alone was 57.6% of all capabilities per fresh_blood_injector.py's own comments), the system needs a gate that only integrates capabilities into live/materialised status when they demonstrate measurable system improvement. Capabilities that fail evaluation must be explicitly marked useless (not silently ignored) and removed from future integration attempts permanently, rather than being retried indefinitely by the picker.
target_kpi: After N materialiser ticks, the ratio of capabilities marked runtime_mode='rejected_permanent' to total evaluated capabilities is > 0, proving the gate is actively filtering, and the live-module success rate (post-integration verification pass rate) trends upward over a rolling 7-day window
acceptance_criteria: Define 'measurable system improvement' concretely: e.g. passes capability_verifier.py's post-integration checks AND produces a non-zero delta on at least one tracked KPI (from kpi_evaluator.py or kpi_cache.json)
Add a new runtime_mode value (e.g. 'rejected_permanent') that the picker query explicitly excludes going forward
Build the evaluator as a standalone module that can be invoked per-capability post-materialisation
Emit a report of rejected vs accepted capabilities, queryable via a new admin endpoint
source_docs: task brief (new user requirement, no prior planning doc)
blocker: Needs a design doc first — 'measurable system improvement' must be defined concretely before code can be written; also needs a live materialiser producing modules to evaluate against
notes: The evaluator logic itself could plausibly be a net-new module, but wiring it into the picker/materialiser pipeline to actually exclude rejected capabilities requires touching existing selection logic in capability_materialiser.py/capability_promoter.py, which is a semantics change, not net-new. Hence 'partial'.

name: Knowledge-graph 'Active' badge measures wrong thing
description: Dashboard shows Nodes: 27710 / Synapses: 30025 / Active: 54 — but 'Active' is not measuring node activation. It's counting green provider/component health-check pings (see static/dashboard.html lines 2173, 2198: n.active = active.has(pid) OR comps[ckey] !== false). Real node activation (P6_AdvancedIntelligence: sum(a > 0.5 for a in activations.values())) is never plumbed to the badge. Fix: either (a) split into 3 separate badges — Providers Active / Components Active / Neurons Firing — or (b) compute real neuron activation from the P6 activations dict and route that to brainActiveCount. Same class of bug as SI 67% vs 0.005% dashboard mismatch.
target_kpi: Dashboard 'Active' badge shows a value with the same denominator as Nodes (27,710) — i.e. count of neurons with activation > 0.5 — not the intersection of provider health pings.
acceptance_criteria: Badge label clarifies what is being counted (renamed or split)
If neuron activation used: value ranges 0..27710 and reflects P6_AdvancedIntelligence activations dict
No console errors on dashboard load
Old provider/component health count still surfaced somewhere (do not lose observability)
notes: UI file is off-limits to self-gen (Issue #218 scope boundary) — Workflow B: DMAI drafts the fix in a sandbox branch, tests, opens [DMAI-DRAFT] PR, waits for human merge.
